message:
How it reads now:
Contracts sheet
Customer (text, required), Value a year (money, required), Start (date), Renews on (date, Start + 1 year), Notice (days, 30), Owner (person, whoever adds it), Signed contract (file).
The form: Basics (Customer, Value a year and Owner), Dates (Start, Renews on and Notice), Documents (Signed contract). Asked when creating: Customer, Value a year and Start.

Renewals sheet
Contract (one row from Contracts, required), Due (date), New value a year (money), Decision (Renew or End), Notes (long text).

Contacts sheet
Contract (one row from Contracts, required), Name (text, required), Role (text), Email (email), Phone (phone).

Steps
Draft → Signed → Active → Renewal due → Renewed or Ended

What happens by itself
60 days before a contract’s notice date, move it to Renewal due and remind its owner.
30 days before the notice date, if it is still in Renewal due, tell Wade and the owner.
When a signed PDF is added, an AI step reads it and fills the row for the owner to confirm; then it moves to Signed.

Who can see and do what
Wade Wilson and Krishna see every contract, add, edit and move them, and change how it works.
Contract owners see their own contracts and can edit and move them.
Everyone else sees nothing.

Connections
People fills Owner.

Coming soon
Connections to other software

This chat so far:
Wade Wilson: Split the contract form into Basics, Dates and Documents.
Bike: (sent a preview)
Wade Wilson: Apply
Bike: Applying the change to Customer contracts. This takes a few seconds.
Wade Wilson: Also ask for the start date when a contract is added.
Bike: (sent a preview)
Wade Wilson: Apply
Bike: Applying the change to Customer contracts. This takes a few seconds.

Latest message from Wade Wilson:
Only ask for the customer and the value when a contract is added.
